title: Enterprise RAG Prospector: buyer interviews + switch-cost micro-simulator for low-latency model selection
creator: Asha Menon
description: Objective: Run a focused product + market research sprint to (1) synthesize enterprise buyer priorities for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) use cases that are latency sensitive and (2) produce a lightweight simulator that estimates commercial and operational switch-costs when moving between model variants (hosted, dedicated, private) under latency constraints. Deliverables: interview synthesis (20 enterprise buyers / platform engineers), a switch-cost micro-simulator (spreadsheet + reproducible notebook), a decision rubric for recommended model fallbacks for low-latency RAG flows, and a prioritized set of procurement triggers for sales/solutions engineering. Rationale: Many customers price latency and availability differently; we need empirical buyer signals + a quantitative simulation to align product trade-offs (e.g., dedicated capacity vs quantized hosted variant) with procurement/contracts and Console rollout controls.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Kickoff: Aligned with Solutions Eng and GTM. Agreed scope: 20 interviews (mix of SRE, ML infra, product), focus on RAG workflows where end-to-end query latency > critical threshold. Diego to draft interview guide.

2025-02-20 - Interview guide v0.1 posted to Confluence: sections cover SLA tolerances, fallback tolerances, switch decision drivers (cost, procurement friction, security), and historical outage pain points. Link in 'links' field below.

2025-02-24 - Fielding plan approved: 12 existing enterprise contacts (Solutions Eng outreach) + 8 cold interviews (sales-sourced). Each interview target 30 minutes. Incentives approved (gift cards for cold interviews).

2025-02-27 - Simulator design: Diego prototyped a micro-simulator that models per-request token cost, latency distribution by model variant, procurement lag (contract negotiation days), and migration engineering effort (person-weeks). Prototype spreadsheet attached.

2025-03-03 - Early synthesis from 7 interviews: recurring themes: (a) predictable p95 latency >> single-model benchmarking, (b) procurement unwillingness to accept multi-vendor rollbacks without fallback guarantees, (c) preference for automated fallbacks integrated into Console. Draft recommendations in comments below.
2025-03-05 - Blockers: Need quantized model latency profiles for two candidate open models. Action: Eng infra (ENG-1984) to run calibration microbenchmarks across sequence lengths by 2025-03-10.
Reviewer feedback (2025-03-05): PM lead Jin Park: include legal/compliance column in switch-cost model for Private/VPC deployments. Added as dependency to legal review ticket.
acceptance_criteria: 20 completed interview notes (anonymized) uploaded to Confluence
Switch-cost micro-simulator with parameterized inputs (latency distributions, token cost, procurement lag, eng effort) delivered as reproducible notebook + spreadsheet
Decision rubric that maps workload profile -> recommended fallback strategy (hosted quantized variant / dedicated reserved pool / private deployment) with expected delta in cost and p95 latency
A one-page briefing for Sales & Solutions Eng with three procurement triggers and recommended Console rollout controls
notes: Trade-offs under study: end-to-end p95 latency vs TCO; engineering effort to support cross-model KV cache migration; SLA/contractual burden of multi-variant fallbacks
Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per request, procurement lead days, eng person-weeks for migration, probability of graceful fallback success
Experiment plan: run microbenchmarks across sequence lengths [8,32,128,512], measure throughput-latency curves for candidate quantized models and dedicated pool shapes
Deliverable timeline: interviews complete by 2025-03-21, simulator v1 by 2025-03-28, briefing to Sales by 2025-04-04
